paragraph_reviews.text: For eight weeks, I tried a morning routine: reading a chapter before looking at my phone. I expected it to help me remember more of what I read. At the end, I could recall the plots of three novels, but I had not tested my memory before the experiment, so I cannot tell whether my recall actually improved.
paragraph_reviews.assessment: Trial routine, expected memory benefit and missing pre-test. Reviewed against the original source; no required fidelity or comprehension repair. Source-constraint anchors: R01, R02, R03.

paragraph_reviews.text: The change I noticed was simpler: I stopped interrupting a chapter to check messages. I liked that. I still checked my phone as soon as I finished. I did not follow the routine consistently: on two mornings I skipped reading altogether.
paragraph_reviews.assessment: Reduced interruption, liking, later phone check and inconsistent adherence. Reviewed against the original source; no required fidelity or comprehension repair. Source-constraint anchors: R04, R05.

paragraph_reviews.text: My mornings were quiet during those weeks, and I did not try the routine when I was travelling, so I am reluctant to recommend it to everyone.
